transaction_order_semantics: SQLite ledger sequence is authoritative transaction order. Caller timestamps are normalized to UTC at admission and remain metadata. Valid-time intervals determine real-world applicability.
witness_semantics: Witnesses are typed as event:<event_id> or external:<authority>:<id>. Ledger witnesses must exist by atomic batch commit. A promotion must have at least one observed event in its transitive parent/witness closure.
compatibility_semantics: Artifact reads require an active runtime policy. Base-weight, component, ontology, and verifier versions are exact by default. Older versions are accepted only by an explicit registered compatibility or ontology-migration rule.

mechanisms.name: typed witness closure and promotion grounding gate
authoritative_inputs: typed event or external provenance witnesses
assumptions: observed is the only speech act that creates an empirical root
external witnesses do not automatically convert inferred or synthetic events into observations
atomic batches may contain forward witness references resolved within that batch
mechanisms.scope: durable promotion events marked by payload.promotion
mechanisms.cost: O(events plus parent/witness edges) per promotion batch
mechanisms.tradeoff: strict grounding rejects potentially useful synthetic capabilities until an observed root is linked
mechanisms.failure_response: roll back the entire event batch and retain the candidate as non-promoted working state
kill_criteria: G1: an event:<id> witness absent from the atomic batch and ledger is accepted
G2: a synthetic/inferred-only promotion is accepted
G3: a grounded multi-hop promotion is rejected
G4: an external witness attached to an inferred event is counted as an observed root
G5: promotion rejection exposes a partial batch

mechanisms.name: ledger-sequence transaction order with normalized timestamps
assumptions: one SQLite authority assigns append sequence
backdated metadata cannot rewrite append order
mechanisms.cost: constant-time timestamp normalization and O(events) replay
mechanisms.tradeoff: late-arriving historical events preserve their old valid time but are still later transactions
mechanisms.failure_response: reject naive or invalid timestamps; use sequence rather than lexical timestamp comparison
permitted_mutations: canonicalize timestamp fields before event hashing
kill_criteria: T1: equal instants with different offsets serialize differently
T2: a backdated later append appears before an earlier ledger sequence
T3: valid-time filtering reads transaction order as world validity
T4: replay of one ledger frontier is nondeterministic

mechanisms.name: fail-closed artifact runtime compatibility
authoritative_inputs: registered component compatibility and ontology migration rules
outputs: compatible artifact read or typed incompatibility failure
assumptions: compatibility is directional from stored artifact version to active runtime
absence of a rule means incompatible
mechanisms.scope: base-weight, component, ontology, and verifier versions on every ArtifactEnvelope read
mechanisms.cost: O(number of stamped components) per read
mechanisms.tradeoff: fail-closed defaults cause rebuilds until compatibility is explicitly registered
mechanisms.failure_response: reject the artifact and rebuild; never silently treat a stale ontology as current
permitted_mutations: register a reviewed directional compatibility rule
kill_criteria: C1: an artifact reads without an active runtime policy
C2: a component mismatch reads without a registered rule
C3: an ontology mismatch reads without a registered migration
C4: a registered compatible predecessor is rejected
C5: verifier incompatibility is downgraded to a warning
